title: introduce-nonblocking-heartbeat-and-graceful-shutdown-session-facade
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat: add HB-1 heartbeat wire extension and client/server hooks
refactor: unify session facade across Python/TS/Go SDKs
feat(test): add flaky-network harness and deterministic time mock
fix: ensure runtime drain path doesn't spin under backpressure
description: Context and motivation: Customers using long-lived streaming sessions reported hard-to-diagnose hangs during transient infra disruptions and application shutdowns. This PR implements a non-blocking heartbeat protocol extension (HB-1), a cross-SDK session facade that exposes explicit graceful shutdown primitives, and ergonomic helpers per-language so consumers can signal cancel/close without leaking goroutines/async tasks. Summary of changes: adds HB-1 control frame and processing on the server; introduces SessionFacade abstraction in each SDK with Start/Heartbeat/Drain/Close (sync + async variants); adds client-side backpressure hints that let the runtime prioritize draining cached KV frames; exposes graceful shutdown integrations: Python contextmanager/asynccontext, TypeScript AbortSignal friendly close(), Go CloseNotifier and WaitForDrain; adds telemetry points (session.heartbeat.sent, session.drain.start, session.drain.complete, session.shutdown.error) and ties them into console dashboards. Testing and validation: new integration harness that simulates packet loss, delayed ACKs, and process SIGTERM; unit tests for state transitions; cross-sdk interoperability test matrix to verify HB-1 negotiation and fallback to baseline heartbeat behavior. Checklist: - [x] Design doc posted in Linear (ENG-8451); - [x] Wire protocol draft reviewed by infra and SRE; - [x] SDK implementations for Python/TS/Go added; - [x] Backwards compatibility: negotiate HB-1 and fall back when peer does not support it; - [x] Telemetry and dashboard tiles created. Rollout plan: feature gated behind the runtime flag "enable_session_facade"; default off in hosted for two weeks then opt-in canary; SDKs ship minor bumps informing users how to opt into explicit shutdown flows. Impact and risk: reduces leaking client tasks during shutdown and provides SRE better visibility into stuck streams; risk is low if gating and fallbacks are respected. Related: ENG-8622 (runtime drain path improvements), SUP-4221 (customer incident reproducer).
